items.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: I was listening to other people and a little, you know like maybe Bud Shank at that time or Vinnie Dean or Lee Konitz, that kind of thing he did with Stan or even the tenor players with Woody’s band.

ctx.x: What was Marshall Royal like? Was he an exacting straw boss?

Well he was a straw boss, you got that right. I don’t know, I love Marshall. Marshall never really dictated, Marshall did it the way a real lead player should do it, and it’s the way I’ve always advocated. You shouldn’t have to tell people anything. You just play it the way you want it and they should follow you. And that’s what he did. And everybody had enough respect for him that they did it. To be very honest with you I didn’t agree © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

with everything Marshall played. I mean the way he played is not my style of playing. And I didn’t listen to him that much when I was a kid, I was listening to other people and a little, you know like maybe Bud Shank at that time or Vinnie Dean or Lee Konitz, that kind of thing he did with Stan or even the tenor players with Woody’s band.
